source.method: chapter (unit) titles from each book's Contents page; topics from each chapter PDF's numbered section and subsection headings (Summary and Exercises are not topics; small neighbouring subsections are grouped under one topic; long 'Chemical Reactions' sections are split by the reaction classes the section itself names, keeping the heading words in the topic title)

topics.title: Types of Solutions
objectives: Student can define a solution as a homogeneous mixture and identify solute and solvent
Student can classify binary solutions by the physical states of solute and solvent with examples
visualIdeas: 3 x 3 grid of solid, liquid and gas solutes in solid, liquid and gas solvents

topics.title: Expressing Concentration of Solutions: Percentages and Parts per Million
objectives: Student can express concentration as mass percentage, volume percentage and mass by volume percentage
Student can express trace concentrations in parts per million and calculate them
visualIdeas: beaker with solute and solvent masses labelled

topics.title: Expressing Concentration of Solutions: Mole Fraction, Molarity and Molality
objectives: Student can calculate mole fraction and show that the mole fractions in a solution add up to one
Student can calculate molarity and molality of a solution
Student can explain why mass %, ppm, mole fraction and molality do not depend on temperature while molarity does
visualIdeas: worked example of ethylene glycol in water converted between units

topics.title: Solubility of a Solid in a Liquid
objectives: Student can define solubility and explain "like dissolves like"
Student can explain dissolution and crystallisation reaching dynamic equilibrium in a saturated solution
Student can describe how temperature and pressure affect the solubility of a solid in a liquid
visualIdeas: saturated solution with dissolution and crystallisation arrows in balance

topics.title: Solubility of a Gas in a Liquid
objectives: Student can state Henry's law, p = KH x, and relate the Henry's law constant to solubility
Student can apply Henry's law to soft drinks, scuba diving (bends) and anoxia at high altitude
Student can explain why the solubility of gases in liquids decreases with rise in temperature
visualIdeas: gas above a liquid compressed to increase dissolved molecules
scuba diver with nitrogen bubbles in blood

topics.title: Vapour Pressure of Liquid-Liquid Solutions
objectives: Student can state Raoult's law for a solution of two volatile liquids
Student can use Dalton's law to find the total vapour pressure and the composition of the vapour phase
Student can explain Raoult's law as a special case of Henry's law
visualIdeas: plot of p1, p2 and total vapour pressure against mole fraction

topics.title: Vapour Pressure of Solutions of Solids in Liquids
objectives: Student can explain why adding a non-volatile solute lowers the vapour pressure of the solvent
Student can apply Raoult's law in its general form to a solution of a non-volatile solute
visualIdeas: surface of a solvent partly covered by solute particles, fewer molecules escaping

topics.title: Ideal and Non-ideal Solutions
objectives: Student can define ideal solutions with Delta_mix H = 0 and Delta_mix V = 0
Student can explain positive and negative deviations from Raoult's law in terms of A-B interactions, with examples
Student can explain minimum and maximum boiling azeotropes such as ethanol-water and nitric acid-water

topics.title: Relative Lowering of Vapour Pressure
objectives: Student can define colligative properties as those depending on the number of solute particles
Student can derive the relative lowering of vapour pressure equal to the mole fraction of the solute
Student can calculate the molar mass of a solute from vapour pressure data
visualIdeas: vapour pressure of pure solvent vs solution

topics.title: Elevation of Boiling Point

Student can calculate molar mass of a solute from boiling point elevation

topics.title: Depression of Freezing Point
objectives: Student can explain why a solution freezes at a lower temperature than the pure solvent
Student can use Delta Tf = Kf m and define the cryoscopic constant
Student can calculate the freezing point of a solution such as ethylene glycol in water
visualIdeas: vapour pressure curves showing the lowered freezing point

topics.title: Osmosis and Osmotic Pressure

topics.title: Chemical Reactions: Cleavage of O-H Bond
objectives: Student can show the acidic nature of alcohols and phenols by their reaction with metals
Student can explain why phenol is more acidic than ethanol and how substituents change phenol acidity
Student can describe esterification of alcohols and phenols
visualIdeas: resonance-stabilised phenoxide ion
pKa ladder of ethanol, water, phenol and nitrophenols

topics.title: Chemical Reactions: Cleavage of C-O Bond in Alcohols
objectives: Student can describe reactions of alcohols with hydrogen halides (Lucas test) and phosphorus trihalides
Student can explain acid-catalysed dehydration of alcohols and its mechanism
Student can describe oxidation and dehydrogenation of primary, secondary and tertiary alcohols
visualIdeas: ethanol dehydration mechanism step by step

topics.title: Reactions of Phenols
objectives: Student can describe electrophilic substitution in phenol: nitration and halogenation
Student can write Kolbe's reaction and the Reimer-Tiemann reaction
Student can describe reaction of phenol with zinc dust and its oxidation
visualIdeas: phenol with ortho and para positions activated by -OH

topics.title: Some Commercially Important Alcohols
objectives: Student can describe the manufacture and uses of methanol and ethanol
Student can explain why methanol is poisonous and what denatured alcohol is
visualIdeas: fermentation of molasses to ethanol

topics.title: Preparation of Ethers
objectives: Student can prepare ethers by acid dehydration of alcohols and explain its limitations
Student can describe Williamson synthesis and choose suitable halide and alkoxide
visualIdeas: Williamson synthesis SN2 attack of alkoxide on an alkyl halide

topics.title: Physical Properties of Ethers
objectives: Student can compare boiling points of ethers with alkanes and alcohols of similar mass
Student can explain the solubility of ethers in water
visualIdeas: ether molecule hydrogen-bonded to water but not to itself

topics.title: Chemical Reactions of Ethers
objectives: Student can describe cleavage of the C-O bond in ethers by hydrogen halides and predict the products
Student can describe electrophilic substitution in anisole: halogenation, Friedel-Crafts reaction and nitration
visualIdeas: anisole with methoxy group directing ortho and para

topics.title: Nomenclature and Structure of Carbonyl Group
objectives: Student can name aldehydes and ketones by common and IUPAC systems
Student can describe the planar, polar carbonyl group with sp2 carbon and its resonance structures
visualIdeas: carbonyl group with sigma and pi bonds and partial charges

topics.title: Preparation of Aldehydes and Ketones
objectives: Student can prepare aldehydes and ketones by oxidation and dehydrogenation of alcohols
Student can prepare them from hydrocarbons by ozonolysis of alkenes and hydration of alkynes
visualIdeas: reaction map from alcohols and hydrocarbons to carbonyl compounds

topics.title: Preparation of Aldehydes
objectives: Student can prepare aldehydes from acyl chlorides (Rosenmund reduction) and from nitriles and esters (Stephen reaction, DIBAL-H)
Student can prepare aromatic aldehydes from hydrocarbons by Etard reaction, side-chain chlorination and Gatterman-Koch reaction
visualIdeas: toluene to benzaldehyde by chromyl chloride

topics.title: Preparation of Ketones
objectives: Student can prepare ketones from acyl chlorides with dialkylcadmium and from nitriles with Grignard reagents
Student can prepare aromatic ketones by Friedel-Crafts acylation
visualIdeas: benzene acylated to acetophenone

topics.title: Physical Properties of Aldehydes and Ketones
objectives: Student can compare boiling points of aldehydes and ketones with hydrocarbons, ethers and alcohols of similar mass
Student can explain solubility of lower aldehydes and ketones in water
visualIdeas: dipole-dipole attraction between carbonyl molecules

topics.title: Chemical Reactions: Nucleophilic Addition Reactions
objectives: Student can describe the mechanism of nucleophilic addition to the carbonyl group
Student can explain why aldehydes are more reactive than ketones
Student can write addition of HCN, sodium hydrogensulphite, Grignard reagents and alcohols (hemiacetals, acetals)
Student can write addition-elimination reactions with ammonia derivatives to give oximes, hydrazones and semicarbazones
visualIdeas: nucleophile attacking trigonal carbonyl carbon giving a tetrahedral intermediate

topics.title: Chemical Reactions: Reduction and Oxidation
objectives: Student can reduce aldehydes and ketones to alcohols and to hydrocarbons by Clemmensen and Wolff-Kishner reductions
Student can distinguish aldehydes from ketones with Tollens' and Fehling's tests
Student can describe the haloform reaction of methyl ketones
visualIdeas: silver mirror in a Tollens' test tube and red precipitate in Fehling's test

topics.title: Chemical Reactions: Reactions due to Alpha-Hydrogen and Other Reactions
objectives: Student can explain the acidity of alpha-hydrogens
Student can describe aldol condensation and cross aldol condensation
Student can describe the Cannizzaro reaction and electrophilic substitution in aromatic aldehydes and ketones
visualIdeas: two ethanal molecules joining in an aldol reaction

topics.title: Uses of Aldehydes and Ketones
objectives: Student can list uses of formaldehyde (formalin), acetaldehyde, benzaldehyde and acetone
Student can name aldehydes and ketones used in flavours and perfumes
visualIdeas: bottles of formalin and acetone with their uses

topics.title: Nomenclature and Structure of Carboxyl Group
objectives: Student can name carboxylic acids by common and IUPAC systems
Student can describe the structure of the carboxyl group and explain why it is less electrophilic than a carbonyl
visualIdeas: resonance structures of the carboxyl group

topics.title: Methods of Preparation of Carboxylic Acids
objectives: Student can prepare carboxylic acids from primary alcohols, aldehydes and alkylbenzenes by oxidation
Student can prepare them from nitriles and amides, from Grignard reagents and from acyl halides, anhydrides and esters
visualIdeas: reaction map of routes to carboxylic acids

topics.title: Physical Properties of Carboxylic Acids
objectives: Student can explain the high boiling points of carboxylic acids by hydrogen-bonded dimers
Student can explain the solubility of lower acids in water
visualIdeas: carboxylic acid dimer with two hydrogen bonds

topics.title: Chemical Reactions: Reactions Involving Cleavage of O-H Bond
objectives: Student can show the acidity of carboxylic acids by their reactions with metals and alkalies
Student can explain why carboxylic acids are stronger than phenols and alcohols using carboxylate resonance
Student can explain the effect of electron-withdrawing and electron-donating groups on acidity
visualIdeas: carboxylate ion with negative charge shared equally over two oxygens

topics.title: Chemical Reactions: Reactions Involving Cleavage of C-OH Bond
objectives: Student can describe formation of anhydrides and esterification
Student can describe reactions with PCl5, PCl3 and SOCl2, and with ammonia to form amides
visualIdeas: ethanoic acid converted to ester, acid chloride and amide

topics.title: Chemical Reactions: Reactions Involving -COOH Group and Substitution in the Hydrocarbon Part
objectives: Student can describe reduction of carboxylic acids and decarboxylation
Student can describe the Hell-Volhard-Zelinsky reaction and ring substitution in aromatic acids
visualIdeas: alpha-halogenation of a carboxylic acid

topics.title: Uses of Carboxylic Acids
objectives: Student can list uses of methanoic acid, ethanoic acid (vinegar) and hexanedioic acid (nylon-6,6)
Student can state uses of benzoic acid esters in perfumery, sodium benzoate as a food preservative and higher fatty acids in soaps and detergents
visualIdeas: vinegar, food preservative and soap with the acids they contain

topics.title: Structure and Classification of Amines
objectives: Student can describe the pyramidal shape of amines with an sp3 nitrogen and a lone pair
Student can classify amines as primary, secondary and tertiary, and as aliphatic or aromatic
visualIdeas: pyramidal trimethylamine with lone pair
primary, secondary and tertiary amines side by side

topics.title: Nomenclature
objectives: Student can name aliphatic amines by common names (alkylamines) and IUPAC names (alkanamines)
Student can name arylamines, such as aniline (benzenamine), and substituted anilines
visualIdeas: amines with common and IUPAC names

topics.title: Preparation of Amines: Reduction and Ammonolysis
objectives: Student can prepare amines by reduction of nitro compounds, nitriles and amides
Student can prepare amines by ammonolysis of alkyl halides and explain why it gives a mixture
visualIdeas: nitrobenzene reduced to aniline with Sn/HCl

topics.title: Preparation of Amines: Gabriel Phthalimide Synthesis and Hoffmann Bromamide Degradation
objectives: Student can describe Gabriel phthalimide synthesis of primary amines and why it cannot make aromatic amines
Student can describe Hoffmann bromamide degradation and the loss of one carbon atom
visualIdeas: phthalimide alkylated and hydrolysed to a primary amine

topics.title: Physical Properties of Amines
objectives: Student can explain hydrogen bonding and boiling points of primary, secondary and tertiary amines
Student can explain the solubility of lower amines in water
visualIdeas: hydrogen bonds between amine molecules

topics.title: Chemical Reactions: Basic Character of Amines
objectives: Student can explain why amines are basic and form salts with acids
Student can compare basic strengths of aliphatic amines in gas phase and water using inductive, solvation and steric effects
Student can explain why aryl amines are weaker bases than ammonia using resonance
visualIdeas: pKb ladder of ammonia, methylamines and aniline

topics.title: Chemical Reactions: Alkylation, Acylation, Carbylamine Reaction and Reaction with Nitrous Acid
objectives: Student can write alkylation and acylation (including benzoylation) of amines
Student can use the carbylamine reaction as a test for primary amines
Student can describe the reaction of aliphatic and aromatic primary amines with nitrous acid
visualIdeas: primary amine with chloroform and KOH giving a foul-smelling isocyanide

topics.title: Chemical Reactions: Reaction with Arylsulphonyl Chloride and Electrophilic Substitution
objectives: Student can use Hinsberg's reagent to distinguish primary, secondary and tertiary amines
Student can explain bromination, nitration and sulphonation of aniline and why the -NH2 group is protected by acetylation
visualIdeas: aniline giving 2,4,6-tribromoaniline with bromine water

topics.title: Method of Preparation and Physical Properties of Diazonium Salts
objectives: Student can prepare benzenediazonium chloride by diazotisation of aniline at 273-278 K
Student can explain why arenediazonium salts are more stable than alkyldiazonium salts and are used in solution
visualIdeas: aniline in ice bath with NaNO2 and HCl

topics.title: Chemical Reactions of Diazonium Salts
objectives: Student can write reactions involving displacement of nitrogen: Sandmeyer and Gatterman reactions and replacement by I, F, H, OH and NO2
Student can write coupling reactions with phenol and aniline that retain the diazo group to form azo dyes
visualIdeas: diazonium salt at the centre of arrows to many products
orange azo dye from coupling with phenol

topics.title: Importance of Diazonium Salts in Synthesis of Aromatic Compounds
objectives: Student can explain how diazonium salts introduce groups like -F, -I, -CN and -OH that cannot be added by direct substitution
Student can plan simple conversions through a diazonium salt
visualIdeas: synthesis route from benzene to iodobenzene via aniline

topics.title: Classification of Carbohydrates
objectives: Student can define carbohydrates as optically active polyhydroxy aldehydes or ketones or compounds that give them on hydrolysis
Student can classify carbohydrates as monosaccharides, oligosaccharides and polysaccharides, and as reducing or non-reducing sugars
Student can classify monosaccharides as aldoses or ketoses by carbon number
visualIdeas: tree diagram of carbohydrate classes

topics.title: Monosaccharides: Glucose
objectives: Student can describe the preparation of glucose from sucrose and from starch
Student can use reactions of glucose to establish its open chain structure
Student can explain why the open chain cannot explain all properties and describe the cyclic alpha and beta pyranose forms
visualIdeas: open chain and Haworth ring structures of glucose

topics.title: Monosaccharides: Fructose
objectives: Student can describe fructose as a ketohexose obtained with glucose by hydrolysis of sucrose
Student can draw the open chain and cyclic furanose structures of fructose
visualIdeas: Haworth structure of fructofuranose

topics.title: Disaccharides
objectives: Student can describe the glycosidic linkage joining two monosaccharides
Student can describe sucrose, maltose and lactose, their hydrolysis products and reducing nature
Student can explain why hydrolysis of sucrose gives invert sugar
visualIdeas: sucrose drawn as glucose and fructose joined by a glycosidic bond

topics.title: Polysaccharides
objectives: Student can describe starch (amylose and amylopectin), cellulose and glycogen and the linkages in them
Student can explain the importance of carbohydrates to plants and animals
visualIdeas: straight chain amylose vs branched amylopectin

topics.title: Amino Acids
objectives: Student can describe alpha-amino acids and their zwitterion form
Student can classify amino acids as acidic, basic or neutral, and as essential or non-essential
visualIdeas: zwitterion of glycine
table of amino acids with three-letter codes

topics.title: Structure of Proteins
objectives: Student can describe the peptide bond and distinguish fibrous and globular proteins
Student can describe primary, secondary (alpha-helix and beta-pleated sheet), tertiary and quaternary structures
visualIdeas: alpha-helix and beta-pleated sheet models

topics.title: Denaturation of Proteins
objectives: Student can explain denaturation as loss of 3D structure and biological activity by heat or pH change
Student can give examples such as coagulation of egg white on boiling and curdling of milk
visualIdeas: egg white turning opaque on boiling

topics.title: Enzymes
objectives: Student can describe enzymes as biocatalysts that are globular proteins
Student can explain that enzymes lower the activation energy of reactions
visualIdeas: enzyme lowering the energy barrier of a reaction

topics.title: Vitamins
objectives: Student can classify vitamins as fat soluble and water soluble
Student can match vitamins with their sources and deficiency diseases
visualIdeas: table of vitamins, sources and deficiency diseases

topics.title: Nucleic Acids
objectives: Student can describe the composition of DNA and RNA: sugar, phosphate and bases
Student can describe nucleosides, nucleotides and the double helix structure of DNA with complementary base pairing
Student can state the biological functions of nucleic acids in heredity and protein synthesis
visualIdeas: DNA double helix with A-T and G-C pairs

topics.title: Hormones
objectives: Student can describe hormones as chemical messengers and give examples of their types
Student can relate hormones such as insulin, thyroxine and steroid hormones to their functions
visualIdeas: endocrine glands releasing hormones into the blood
